extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Extract canonical definitions, equivalent characterizations, and key theorems about smooth, unramified, and étale morphisms of schemes, together with related results on generic smoothness, Kleiman-Bertini, and cohomology-and-base-change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: smooth morphism (Definition 13.6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: π : X → Y is smooth of relative dimension n (Definition 13.6.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the canonical definition used in the text; Theorem 25.2.2 shows a number of equivalent characterizations. See Definition 13.6.2 for the precise original formulation (local description as étale-locally projection An → Spec B, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired Alternate Definition for smooth (25.1.5 / Theorem 25.2.2(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: π is locally of finite presentation, π is flat of relative dimension n, and Ω_{X/Y} is locally free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text calls this a 'desired alternate definition' and Theorem 25.2.2 proves it is equivalent to the canonical Definition 13.6.2. Useful for checking smoothness via cotangent sheaf and flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate characterization: smooth via fibers (Theorem 25.2.2(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: π is locally finitely presented and flat, and the fibers are smooth k-schemes of pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to smoothness of relative dimension n (Theorem 25.2.2). This gives a fiberwise regularity/geometry test for smoothness after verifying flatness and finite presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate characterization: smooth via geometric fibers (Theorem 25.2.2(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: π is locally finitely presented and flat, and the geometric fibers are smooth k-schemes of pure dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also equivalent to smoothness. In some proofs (e.g., over nonperfect fields) geometric fibers are the correct notion to use; Exercise 13.2.H links (iii) and (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale characterization (Desired Alternate Definition 25.1.5 and Exercise 25.2.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: π is étale if and only if π is locally of finite presentation, flat, and Ω_{π} = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the alternate/desired characterization of étaleness; Exercise 25.2.B asks to show equivalence with Definition 13.6.2. Compare also with equivalences given in Exercise 25.2.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formally smooth / formally étale / formally unramified (lifting criterion, 25.2.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: π : X → Y is formally smooth (resp. formally étale, formally unramified) if for all affine Z and every closed subscheme Z0 ⊂ Z defined by a nilpotent ideal, the canonical map Hom_Y(Z,X) → Hom_Y(Z0,X) is surjective (resp. bijective, injective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Grothendieck (EGA) style infinitesimal lifting criterion. Replacing 'nilpotent' by 'square-zero' gives an equivalent formulation often easier to work with. Grothendieck’s definitions: smooth = formally smooth + locally of finite presentation, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck-EGA approach: smooth = formally smooth + locally of finite presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: [Gr-EGA] defines smooth (and similarly unramified and étale) as formally smooth plus locally of finite presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text notes this starting point is less geometric but powerful for formal properties (e.g., left-exactness of cotangent sequences) and that these definitions agree with the ones given earlier (references: Gr-EGA, Stacks tag 00TN, 00UO).

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth implies flat (Exercise 25.2.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is smooth of relative dimension n (and either Y is locally Noetherian or one accepts the slicing criterion Remark 24.6.7), then π is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exercise gives a constructive hint: work locally as Spec of a quotient B[x1,...]/(f1,...,fr) and use induction with the slicing criterion for flatness in the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smooth implies regular (25.2.3 / Smoothness-Regularity Comparison Theorem 13.2.7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every smooth k-scheme (of dimension n) is regular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation 13.6.4 and Exercise 13.3.P used: locally express X as an étale cover of An_k which is regular, then apply Exercise 25.2.D (slicing) to deduce regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale <-> smooth and unramified (Exercise 25.2.C equivalences)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π : X → Y, the following are equivalent: (a) π is étale; (b) π is smooth and unramified; (c) π is locally finitely presented, flat, and unramified; (d) π is locally finitely presented, flat, and for each q ∈ Y, π^{-1}(q) is the disjoint union of schemes of the form Spec K where K/κ(q) is finite separable; (e) π is locally finitely presented, flat, and for each geometric point q of Y, π^{-1}(q) is the disjoint union of copies of q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These alternate characterizations give practical checks for étaleness: combine flatness + unramifiedness or examine fiber structure (finite separable field extensions or disjoint geometric copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian criterion for smoothness over a field (used in proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed subscheme U_k ⊂ A^N_k of codimension r, smoothness at a closed point p is detected by the Jacobian matrix: the cotangent/conormal space is cut out by r linear equations and Jacobian rank conditions (Exercise 13.2.E and Theorem 21.2.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the proof of Theorem 25.2.2 to choose generators f1,...,fr whose Jacobian has invertible minor, allowing local description as desired. The text includes Exercise 25.2.H to show those generators generate the ideal locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness on the source (Theorem 25.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field of characteristic 0 and π : X → Y a dominant morphism of integral k-varieties. Then there is a nonempty (dense) open set U ⊂ X such that π|_U is smooth of dimension dim X − dim Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument uses transcendence degree → rank of Ω_{X/Y} at generic point, upper semicontinuity of fiber rank of a coherent sheaf, and generic flatness to find the open set where Ω is locally free of rank n and π is flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness on the target when source is smooth (Theorem 25.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is a morphism of k-varieties with char k = 0 and X smooth over k. Then there is a dense open subset U ⊂ Y such that π|_{π^{-1}(U)} is smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to Y smooth by generic smoothness on source, considers determinantal/rank loci X_r where cotangent map has rank ≤ r, applies Chevalley and dimension bounds (Lemma 25.3.4) to remove bad locus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension bound lemma for rank loci (Lemma 25.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y are finite-type schemes over k (char 0) and X_r = {p ∈ X : rank(π^*Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k}) ≤ r}, then dim π(X_r) ≤ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show the bad locus on the target has smaller dimension; proof uses replacing by irreducible components and generic smoothness on source plus linear algebra rank restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kleiman-Bertini Theorem (25.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose X is a homogeneous space for a group variety G over algebraically closed k of characteristic 0. For morphisms α: Y → X and β: Z → X from smooth k-varieties: (a) there exists a nonempty open V ⊂ G such that for every σ ∈ V(k), the translate Y^σ ×_X Z is smooth of dimension dim Y + dim Z − dim X (possibly empty); (b) there exists a nonempty open V ⊂ G such that the family (G ×_k Y) ×_X Z → V is a smooth morphism of relative dimension dim Y + dim Z − dim X over V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think: for general translate, subvarieties meet transversely. Proof uses generic smoothness on the target twice and G-equivariance/transitivity of action to propagate smoothness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semicontinuity Theorem for cohomology (26.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is proper with Y Noetherian, and F a coherent sheaf on X flat over Y. Then for each p ≥ 0 the function q ↦ dim_{κ(q)} H^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is an upper semicontinuous function on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translates the intuitive statement that ranks of cohomology groups of fibers do not increase in specializations for proper flat families; used to deduce existence of open sets where cohomology ranks are constant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grauert's Theorem (26.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is proper, Y reduced and locally Noetherian, F coherent on X flat over Y, and h^p(X_q, F|_{X_q}) is locally constant in q, then R^pπ_* F is locally free and base-change φ^p_Z is an isomorphism for every ψ: Z → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a partial converse to the fiberwise-isomorphism dream: constancy of fiber cohomology dimensions (on reduced base) implies the higher pushforward is a vector bundle and commutes with arbitrary base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology and Base Change Theorem (26.1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π is proper, Y locally Noetherian, F coherent on X and flat over Y, and φ^p_q (the base-change map at q) is surjective. Then (i) there exists an open neighborhood U of q such that for any ψ: Z → U, φ^p_Z is an isomorphism; (ii)(a) φ^{p-1}_q is surjective iff (ii)(b) R^pπ_* F is locally free in an open neighborhood of q (equivalently (R^pπ_*F)_q is a free O_{Y,q}-module).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This theorem links a pointwise (surjectivity) hypothesis to openness and local freeness of higher pushforwards; Nakayama and the local criterion for flatness are key technical tools. See also consequences/exercises (26.1.C–F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper O-connected morphisms and criterion (26.1.7 and Exercise 26.1.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y is O-connected if the natural map O_Y → π_* O_X is an isomorphism. If π is proper, flat, locally Noetherian, and fibers satisfy h^0(X_q, O_{X_q}) = 1 (e.g., geometrically connected and geometrically reduced fibers), then π is O-connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 26.1.H indicates checking fiber H^0 dimension equals 1, then apply Cohomology-and-Base-Change (φ^0_q surjective ⇒ iso) and Nakayama to conclude π_* O_X ≅ O_Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descent of line bundles under proper O-connected morphism (Proposition 26.1.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π : X → Y is flat, proper, locally Noetherian with geometrically connected and geometrically reduced fibers, Y reduced, and L an invertible sheaf on X trivial on fibers. Then π_* L is locally free of rank 1 on Y (call it M), and the natural map π^* M → L is an isomorphism; i.e., L descends to an invertible sheaf M on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Grauert's theorem to identify fibers H^0 and then checks surjectivity of π^*π_*L → L on fibers; Nakayama and local criteria show the map is an iso. This is the common criterion for descent of line bundles from total space to base in connected proper families.
